target: UTM-bundled QEMU, AArch64 PCI, one vCPU, disposable writable RedSea VirtIO fixture
result: pass: recursive FilesFind reports physical metadata for a nested RedSea directory and file; stock DiskCheck retains both allocations, reclaims the separate orphan, and returns a clean second scan
verified: The disposable 128-sector writable RedSea volume mounts as D with valid bounded geometry.
The root contains SUB at base + 10; SUB contains KEEP.ZC at base + 20; the fixture also has one separate orphan allocation.
FilesFind("D:/*", FUF_RECURSE) returns exactly /SUB and /SUB/KEEP.ZC with the expected attributes, sizes, and physical starting sectors.
The ARM64 ZcRedSeaDirAt bridge returns each directory's physical starting sector and byte length; TaskBridge updates synthesized parent-directory metadata from this pass.
DiskCheck('D', TRUE, FALSE) reclaims only the orphan while preserving the SUB and KEEP.ZC allocation bits.
DiskCheck('D', FALSE, FALSE) then returns zero; final zstatus reports failed=0.
The broader stock-file probe's Drive('D') selection assertion also fails when rerun against the pre-change source at 2285c37, so that failure is not introduced by this patch.
limits: This validates nested allocation preservation and orphan cleanup, not repair of malformed directory contents or directory-entry corruption.
The fixture is a disposable QEMU disk window, not physical SD or USB storage.
FAT32 repair and live UTM UI or Raspberry Pi behavior are not established.
